course.title: Ferry Payments Core
course.description: How money actually moves through Ferry: authorisation, retries, the ledger, FX, compliance and settlement.

_note: Fourteen concepts. Twelve are the original golden-scenario course; `challenge-flow-ux` and `payment-status-communication` were added with the UXD persona (AGCTM-12) so that persona has a topic with a real concept map rather than a label. Prerequisite edges are acyclic; max depth is 3.

concepts.title: Representing money
concepts.description: Minor units, integer arithmetic, why floats lose cents, currency exponents that aren't 2 (JPY, KWD).

concepts.title: Idempotency keys
concepts.description: What an idempotency key protects, what it must cover, how long it lives, and what happens when it expires mid-retry.

concepts.title: Double-entry ledger
concepts.description: Every movement is two postings that sum to zero; balances are derived, postings are immutable.

concepts.title: Payment state machine
concepts.description: Authorised, captured, settled, refunded, disputed — and which transitions are illegal.

concepts.title: Webhook delivery
concepts.description: At-least-once delivery, dedupe on the receiver, ordering guarantees you do not have, and backoff with a cap.

concepts.title: FX quote lifecycle
concepts.description: Quote, spread, expiry, and who carries the risk when a quote expires between authorisation and capture.

concepts.title: Ledger migrations
concepts.description: Backfilling a table nobody may lock: chunked batches, off-peak windows, dry runs against a production snapshot.

concepts.title: Retrying safely
concepts.description: Retrying a payment without charging twice: shared idempotency key, bounded attempts, and telling the customer.

concepts.title: PSP contract testing
concepts.description: Adapter boundaries, recorded fixtures going stale, and detecting provider drift before the provider tells you.

concepts.title: SCA and exemptions
concepts.description: PSD2 strong customer authentication, which exemptions Ferry claims, and the evidence each one requires. Standalone: understanding the regulation does not require the payment state machine, which is why the PM can master it and the engineers have not.

concepts.title: Reconciliation
concepts.description: Matching the bank's settlement file to our ledger, classifying breaks, and why a break is never 'just rounding'.

concepts.title: Payout and settlement
concepts.description: T+2 cutoffs, funding, batching per currency, and what a merchant sees when a payout is short.

concepts.title: Challenge flow: mandated vs chosen
concepts.description: Which parts of the 3DS/SCA challenge screen the regulator requires, which the card scheme requires, and which are Ferry's own product choice — and how to tell them apart when a stakeholder asks to remove a step. Grounded in `checkout-api` (3DS challenge flow) and PAY-1870.

concepts.title: Communicating an uncertain payment
concepts.description: What the customer and the merchant are shown while a payment is retrying, held, or short-paid — and why 'Failed' and 'Not yet succeeded' are different claims. Grounded in PAY-1852 (show retry state to the customer), PAY-1826 and PAY-1869.

related_edges._why: Both are at-least-once problems solved by dedupe. Genuinely confusable, so co-review (core spec, next-item selection step 3) should pull them together.
The challenge is a state in the flow, not a screen bolted onto it. UXD who miss this design a step the state machine cannot reach.
The merchant's view of a payment is whatever the last delivered webhook said. At-least-once delivery is why the UI can show a stale status.
